hints.content: The arrow points to all values less than $3$.
And the point at $3$ is *not* filled in.
So, the inequality represents everything strictly **less than $3$.**

question.content:
**Choose the inequality that represents the following graph.**



[[☃ image 1]]

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the left starts at 3 and continues left. An open point is plotted at 3 where the line begins.

choices.clue:
The graph of $x \leq 3$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the left starts at 3 and continues left. A closed point is plotted at 3 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/3422a6ab42cbdb8bff8a9e6fd6d13132c51e82eb)

The graph of $x > 3$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the right starts at 3 and continues right. An open point is plotted at 3 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/956a58a8e2d50ba79ccdfca4b39e6d7b58ffc011)

The graph of $x \geq 3$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the right starts at 3 and continues right. A closed point is plotted at 3 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/540ca56e1d9f6297cb6979c6939d2ce0e70eee01)
